member.name: F:Math.Comparison.RelativeEpsilon
member.summary: Default relative tolerance for / . Chosen ~3 orders of magnitude looser than so that the absolute tolerance at unit scale (1.0) stays at 1e-13 while large-magnitude values automatically get a proportional tolerance (e.g. 1e-7 m at Earth-radius scale 6.37e6 m).

member.name: M:Math.Comparison.IsEqualRelative(System.Double,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Epsilon-tolerant equality scaled by the larger operand magnitude. Equivalent to |x - y| < relEps * max(|x|, |y|, 1): callers do not have to pre-scale their epsilon when comparing two large numbers (e.g. metres at Earth-radius scale). The unit-scale baseline (the trailing 1) keeps behaviour close to the absolute for small operands. Infinities of the same sign compare equal, just like .

member.name: M:Math.Comparison.IsZeroRelative(System.Double,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Relative-tolerance "is zero" with an explicit reference scale. Returns true iff |x| < relEps * max(|scale|, 1), i.e. is small compared to . Useful for testing residuals of length-scaled quantities (e.g. metres) where the absolute 1e-13 would be meaninglessly tight.

member.name: T:Math.Function
member.summary:
Math facade. The implementation is split across files by responsibility:
Function.Numeric.cs - roots, factorials, Fibonacci, GCD, primes, interpolation
Function.Angles.cs - SinCos, FastSin, NormalizeAngle*
Function.Cycling.cs - cycling-power model (forces, powers, equilibrium velocity)
Function.Energetics.cs - Minetti walking-energy cost model
The partial split is purely organisational; existing callers continue to use Math.Function.Xxx unchanged.

member.name: M:Math.Function.FastSin(System.Double)
member.summary: Cheap polynomial approximation of sin(x) on x in [-pi/2, pi/2] with absolute error < 0.0205.
member.remarks: Outside [-pi/2, pi/2] the polynomial diverges quickly: it is the caller's responsibility to range-reduce the argument first (e.g. via and a half-period reflection). The function does not assert this in release builds to keep "fast" honest, but a debug-only assertion guards against accidental misuse.
